root_motivation: Skill text drifts from installed tooling: skills cite flags and subcommands that have been removed, renamed, or never existed. Claude follows skill prose as ground truth, so drift surfaces as confused tool calls and user-visible errors. The fix has to be machine-checkable (manual audits don't keep up) and review-gated (false positives are inevitable when parsing shell out of Markdown prose).
user_persona: Joe Yen on wintermute, running Claude Code with ~25 SKILL.md files under ~/.claude/skills/. Wants `skill-doctor check` after a `tool-manifest sync` to surface drift as proposals he can promote, reject, or ignore — same idiom as `recall observe`.

acceptance_criteria.description: cargo build --release green; cargo test --release --lib green on a fresh clone
skill-doctor check against live ~/.claude/skills/ produces >=4 drift proposals matching the four live instances in visions/drift.md (or against pre-fix git state if drift-fix landed)
Proposals written under ~/.claude/skill-doctor/proposals/<ULID>.md with the schema in PRD §Proposal output (id, kind, created, status frontmatter + body)
Re-running skill-doctor check does not create duplicates for the same (skill_path, line, binary, drift_kind, detail) tuple; dedup by content hash
skill-doctor proposals reject <ULID> flips status:rejected and the proposal disappears from `proposals list`
Missing tool-manifest is handled gracefully: friendly error directing to `tool-manifest sync`, exit code 2
False-positive rate <=30% on the live skill set: >=70% of proposals reflect real drift (manual review of first batch)
Proposal queue path created with mode 0700 (private to user), matching `recall observe` convention
Published to github.com/j0yen/skill-doctor under dual MIT+Apache-2.0 with README citing drift vision and tool-manifest dependency
~/.local/bin/skill-doctor installed via bootstrap/install.sh and a row in ~/wintermute/REPOS.md
End-to-end loop close: one user-promoted proposal lands as a skill edit (user reviews, runs promote, applies, drift gone)

scope: Extract shell invocations from fenced ```bash/```sh/```shell blocks AND single-line backtick-inline code in prose
Emit drift kinds: BinaryMissing, SubcommandUnknown, FlagUnknown, SkippedVersionOnly
Dedup pending proposals by content hash so re-runs don't accumulate
non_goals: Auto-edit of skill files (Fleet 2 candidate drift-skill-doctor-fix)
Walking config files under ~/.config/** (Fleet 2 candidate drift-config-files)
Parsing multiline backslash-continuations, heredocs, or shell-variable-expanded commands
Shelling out to tool-manifest sync from inside skill-doctor (consumer's responsibility)

five_whys_trace.a: Skill text drifts from installed tooling; we've observed at least four live drift instances (pevent gc --dry-run, pevent gc --older-than 7d type mismatch, bpolicy status --format, missing binaries in self-review's bootstrap-symlinks, ctrace ls in dream).
Claude follows the skill text as ground truth. Stale invocations turn into broken tool calls during /self-review or /dream, surface as user-visible errors, and erode trust in the skill prose.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not catch it manually with grep?
five_whys_trace.a: Skills change frequently enough that a one-off audit goes stale within days. Drift detection must be machine-checkable AND repeatable on demand (skill-doctor check) so it can be wired into self-review later.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a proposal queue instead of auto-editing the skill text?
five_whys_trace.a: Parsing shell out of Markdown prose is inherently noisy; false positives are inevitable. Auto-edit on a noisy detector would corrupt skills. A review-gated queue lets the user accept/reject before any text changes — same trust model as `recall observe`.

The user already has a working mental model for reviewing recall observe's proposal queue. Reusing the same idiom (proposal files, list/show/reject/promote subcommands) lowers cognitive load and reuses any tooling the user has built around that pattern.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should skill-doctor auto-sync the manifest before checking?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No. PRD §Notes for /build: consumers should call `tool-manifest sync` explicitly; skill-doctor reads the JSON file directly. Keeps skill-doctor a pure consumer with no transitive shell-out.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What happens if two skills reference the same drifting invocation?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Write one proposal per occurrence (skill_path+line is part of the dedup tuple), so the user can fix them independently. PRD §Cross-skill diff handling.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What's the relationship to drift-fix-self-review-dream?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Complementary, not blocking. drift-fix closes the four known cases; skill-doctor catches future drift. AC2 may verify against pre-fix git state if drift-fix has already landed.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does AC11 (loop closure) gate publication?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No — AC11 is the verified-completed receipt that proves the loop closes end-to-end. AC1-AC10 gate ship; AC11 is recorded post-ship when the first user-promoted proposal lands.
